newsitem.title: USA: Mercury to acquire BankBoston finance unit.
newsitem.headline: Mercury to acquire BankBoston finance unit.

text.p: Mercury Finance Corp said Friday it signed a definitive agreement to acquire BankBoston Corp's consumer finance subsidiary, Fidelity Acceptance Corp.

Under the agreement, Mercury will issue 32.7 million common shares, or about 16 percent of its total outstanding common shares, to BankBoston. The indicated value of the transaction, expected to be completed during the first quarter of 1997, is $392.5 million.
"We expect the acquisition will be accretive to earnings per share in 1997," Mercury chairman and chief executive officer John Brincat said in a statement.

In connection with the transaction, Mercury, a diversified consumer finance company that buys individual installment sales finance contracts from automobile dealers and retail vendors and extends short-term credit loans, expects to refinance about $700 million of Fidelity Acceptance debt. Salomon Brothers Inc, acting as financial advisor to Mercury, has provided a financing commitment on the debt to be refinanced, the company said.
In connection with the acquisition, Mercury said its previously authorized nine million share repurchase program was increased by its board to 18 million shares.

Brincat said that, at the same time as the acquisition, the company expects to initiate share repurchases "to bring the debt-to-equity ratio of the combined companies more in line with industry norms."
BankBoston, the nation's 15th largest bank holding company with assets of $62 billion as of September 30, 1996, will receive two seats on Mercury's board of directors at the time of closing.

Mercury operates out of 287 offices in 31 state and employs some 1,800 people. Fidelity Acceptance, based in Kansas City, Mo., has 165 offices throughout the U.S. and Guam. The combined company would have about $2.2 billion in net finance receivables.

BankBoston chief executive officer Chad Gifford in a statement said of the transaction: "This action allows our management to focus more intently on our regional consumer business and frees up capital for more productive uses."

Gifford said BankBoston expects to gain from the improvement in Mercury's results arising from the cross selling of their array of insurance, credit cards and consumer loans to a larger combined customer base.

Piper Jaffray analyst Jeffrey Evanson hailed the move by Mercury, noting: "They needed a kick-start to their auto financing business, which has been lagging for the last year. If it's accretive (as the company anticipates), this should be a good move."
Mercury Finance closed Friday on the NYSE at 14, up 1-7/8. BankBoston ended up 1/8 at 65-3/4.
